details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The nearest alternative is implement maintenance as a toggle and retry it when the response is late. It looks like a fresh attempt, but the stem says the caller is replaying the same operation after an uncertain response and gives it a stable identity.
details.transfer: Bind the request identity to the effect whose outcome may be replayed. Reuse it for that same effect, and use a distinct identity for a genuinely new action or revision.

feedback.reason: The command ID tracks one desired-state request rather than each transmission. A later authorized mode change has a different purpose and must not be folded into its retry.

options.text: Return the desired state for this command ID; represent a later mode change separately.
Mint a new ID on timeout; the same maintenance command may run again.
Deduplicate by exhibit ID; a later authorized mode change is blocked.
Send the opposite command when acknowledgement is missing, even if maintenance was set.

prompt: In a museum exhibit controller, each maintenance command has a command ID and desired mode; the controller may change modes before the operator receives an acknowledgement. A later authorized mode change is possible. Which identity policy should govern a retry?
